sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ragged arrays sound fancy, but they're just arrays where each row can have a different length. Think of them like a bookshelf where each shelf holds a different number of books!

• What ragged arrays are and why they're useful
• How to create and use them in Java
• Real-world scenarios where they shine

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine a classroom with different-sized groups of students. One group has 3 students, another has 5, and another has just 2. A regular 2D array would force all groups to have the same number of students (wasting space), but a ragged array lets each group be just the right size!

Here's how it works in Java:
• You create an array of arrays
• Each sub-array can have its own length
• No wasted space for empty slots

Key Points
points: A ragged array is a 2D array where each row can have a different number of columns
Create ragged arrays by initializing each row separately with different sizes
Use matrix[i].length to get the length of each individual row
Ragged arrays are useful for triangular data structures like Pascal's triangle
Nested loops must use matrix[i].length (not a fixed column count) to avoid index errors

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Ragged arrays let you store different amounts of data in each row. Each row must be initialized separately with its own length. Perfect for real-world data that naturally has varying sizes. Practice creating and using them to master multidimensional arrays.

questions.question: What is a ragged array?
options: A 2D array where each row can have a different number of columns
An array that is not initialized
questions.explanation: A ragged (or jagged) array is a 2D array where rows can have different lengths. Each row is an independent array that can be of any size.

questions.question: How do you create a ragged array with 3 rows in Java?
questions.explanation: To create a ragged array, specify only the number of rows: int[][] arr = new int[3][]; Then create each row individually: arr[0] = new int[2]; arr[1] = new int[5]; etc.
